chapter_title: Ethanol Toxicity in the Brain: Alteration of Astroglial Cell Function
source_pdf: /mnt/project-files/Experimental Provenance for QSAR Dataset/Pharmacology (Luca Gallelli) (z-library.sk, 1lib.sk, z-lib.sk).pdf

records.mechanism_book_wording: Nitric oxide (NO) activates guanylilcyclase and increases cytoplasmic cyclic guanosine monophosphate (cGMP) signalling cascades
records.quote: Nitric oxide (NO) activates guanylilcyclase and increases cytoplasmic cyclic guanosine monophosphate (cGMP) signalling cascades
records.notes: Target class (enzyme) is inferred; the page does not use the word enzyme for guanylilcyclase.

records.target: ionotropic and metabotropic receptors (astrocytes and other CNS cell types)
records.role_detail: released messenger that activates receptors (agonism inferred from 'activate ... by acting on')
records.mechanism_book_wording: Released messengers, in turn, activate Ca2+ entry or Ca2+ release from intracellular stores by acting on ionotropic and metabotropic receptors, respectively
records.quote: Released messengers, in turn, activate Ca2+ entry or Ca2+ release from intracellular stores by acting on ionotropic and metabotropic receptors, respectively.
records.notes: The sentence says 'Released messengers'; the next sentence names ATP and glutamate as the major active neurotransmitters. Specific receptor subtypes are not named. Printed page 608 (PDF 620) also mentions 'activation of specific receptors on neighbouring astrocytes' after release of glutamate or ATP.

records.target: ionotropic and metabotropic receptors (astrocytes and other CNS cell types)
records.role_detail: released messenger that activates receptors (agonism inferred from 'activate ... by acting on')
records.mechanism_book_wording: Released messengers, in turn, activate Ca2+ entry or Ca2+ release from intracellular stores by acting on ionotropic and metabotropic receptors, respectively
records.quote: Released messengers, in turn, activate Ca2+ entry or Ca2+ release from intracellular stores by acting on ionotropic and metabotropic receptors, respectively.
records.notes: Same sentence as the ATP record; glutamate is identified as a messenger only by the following sentence ('ATP and glutamate are the major active neurotransmitters'). Receptor subtypes not named.

records.role_detail: named as a Toll-like receptor ligand that triggers reactive astrogliosis; agonism is inferred
records.mechanism_book_wording: mediators of innate immunity such as lipopolysaccharide and other Toll-like receptor ligands
records.quote: mediators of innate immunity such as lipopolysaccharide and other Toll-like receptor ligands
records.notes: The page lists these among signalling molecules able to trigger reactive astrogliosis; it uses the word ligands and does not say agonist. Role is inferred. The sentence does not say that lipopolysaccharide itself is the Toll-like receptor ligand more specifically than 'such as ... and other'.

records.role_detail: increase of enzymatic activity
records.mechanism_book_wording: increasing the enzymatic activities of superoxide-dismutase, catalase, and glutathione-peroxidase
records.quote: increasing the enzymatic activities of superoxide-dismutase, catalase, and glutathione-peroxidase
records.notes: Page words it as ethanol 'induces up-regulation of antioxidant defences by increasing the enzymatic activities'; the mechanism of the increase is not stated.

records.role_detail: increase of enzymatic activity
records.mechanism_book_wording: increasing the enzymatic activities of superoxide-dismutase, catalase, and glutathione-peroxidase
records.quote: increasing the enzymatic activities of superoxide-dismutase, catalase, and glutathione-peroxidase
records.notes: Same sentence as the superoxide-dismutase record. Catalase is also named on this page as a route of ethanol metabolism (substrate, no direction), which is not recorded.

records.role_detail: increase of enzymatic activity
records.mechanism_book_wording: increasing the enzymatic activities of superoxide-dismutase, catalase, and glutathione-peroxidase
records.quote: increasing the enzymatic activities of superoxide-dismutase, catalase, and glutathione-peroxidase
records.notes: Same sentence as the superoxide-dismutase record.

records.role_detail: increased receptor sensitivity (positive modulation); the book does not say agonist, nearest of the two roles chosen
records.mechanism_book_wording: increased sensitivity of glutamate receptors
records.quote: increased sensitivity of glutamate receptors and enhanced trans-membrane transport of glutamate has been observed in the presence of ethanol
records.notes: Role is inferred; this is an observed effect in the presence of ethanol, receptor subtype not named. The accompanying transporter statement (enhanced transmembrane transport of glutamate) is not recorded.

records.role_detail: reduction of endogenous levels of active RhoA (cultured rat astrocytes)
records.mechanism_book_wording: Ethanol reduced endogenous levels of active RhoA
records.quote: Ethanol reduced endogenous levels of acive RhoA due to an increase in the activity of small Rho GTP-ases
records.quote_corrected_reading: Ethanol reduced endogenous levels of active RhoA due to an increase in the activity of small Rho GTP-ases
records.notes: Target class (enzyme) is inferred: RhoA is a small GTPase and the page does not call it an enzyme. Direction is a reduction in the active form, mapped to Inhibitor by inference.

records.role_detail: increase in activity
records.mechanism_book_wording: an increase in the activity of small Rho GTP-ases
records.quote: due to an increase in the activity of small Rho GTP-ases
records.notes: Target class (enzyme) is inferred. The same sentence says active RhoA fell because small Rho GTP-ases increased in activity, which the page does not reconcile; recorded as stated.

records.role_detail: chronic ethanol consumption up-regulates a subunit of the NMDA receptor (expression change, not ligand action); nearest of the two roles chosen
records.mechanism_book_wording: depicted an up-regulation of a subunit of the NMDA receptor
records.quote: and depicted an up-regulation of a subunit of the NMDA receptor
records.notes: Statement is about chronic ethanol consumption (nucleus accumbens, rat). It describes up-regulation of a splice variant subunit, not agonism; rule name is the nearer of Agonist/Antagonist and is a weak fit.

records.role_detail: inhibition of activity, worded as probable cause
records.mechanism_book_wording: probably due to inhibition of plasma membrane Ca2+-ATPase activity
records.quote: Acute exposure of astrocytes to ethanol increases intracellular concentration of Ca2+ ions, probably due to inhibition of plasma membrane Ca2+-ATPase activity
records.notes: Judgement call: Ca2+-ATPase is an ATPase (enzyme) but functions as a pump, so it could be treated as a transporter and filtered out; recorded as enzyme because the page speaks of ATPase activity. The book hedges with 'probably'.

records.role_detail: excitotoxic Ca2+ influx through NMDA-gated channels at high glutamate levels; agonism inferred
records.mechanism_book_wording: high levels of this neurotransmitter lead to excitotoxic neuronal death, mediated by Ca2+ influx, principally through NMDA-gated channels
records.quote: high levels of this neurotransmitter lead to excitotoxic neuronal death, mediated by Ca2+ influx, principally through NMDA-gated channels
records.notes: Target class (receptor) and agonist role are inferred: the page says NMDA-gated channels and does not use the words receptor or agonist here.

records.role_detail: chronic ethanol intake enhances COX-2 (expression/level of inflammatory mediator)
records.mechanism_book_wording: Chronic ethanol intake enhances inflammatory mediators like COX-2, and iNOS
records.quote: Chronic ethanol intake enhances inflammatory mediators like COX-2, and iNOS in rat cerebral cortex and cultured astrocytes.
records.notes: COX-2 is named by abbreviation; enzyme class inferred. The page says enhances mediators (and later 'COX-2 expression'), not enzyme activity; Activator is the nearest role.

records.role_detail: chronic ethanol intake enhances iNOS (expression/level of inflammatory mediator)
records.mechanism_book_wording: Chronic ethanol intake enhances inflammatory mediators like COX-2, and iNOS
records.quote: Chronic ethanol intake enhances inflammatory mediators like COX-2, and iNOS in rat cerebral cortex and cultured astrocytes.
records.notes: iNOS is named by abbreviation (expanded as inducible nitric oxide synthase on printed page 611, PDF 623); enzyme class inferred. Activator is the nearest role for an enhancement.

records.role_detail: stimulation of the IRAK/ERK/NF-kappaB pathway
records.mechanism_book_wording: there is a stimulation of both, interleukin receptor-associated kinase (IRAK)/extracellular signal-regulated kinases (ERK)/nuclear factor-kappaB (NF-kappaB) pathway
records.quote: there is a stimulation of both, interleukin receptor-associated kinase (IRAK)/extracellular signal-regulated kinases (ERK)/nuclear factor-kappaB (NF-kappaB) pathway
records.notes: Pathway-level statement in the section on ethanol and inflammation; the sentence does not repeat the word ethanol, so attribution to ethanol is inferred from the section. Enzyme class (kinase) inferred from the name.

records.role_detail: stimulation of the IRAK/ERK/NF-kappaB pathway
records.mechanism_book_wording: there is a stimulation of both, interleukin receptor-associated kinase (IRAK)/extracellular signal-regulated kinases (ERK)/nuclear factor-kappaB (NF-kappaB) pathway
records.quote: there is a stimulation of both, interleukin receptor-associated kinase (IRAK)/extracellular signal-regulated kinases (ERK)/nuclear factor-kappaB (NF-kappaB) pathway
records.notes: Same sentence as the IRAK record; attribution to ethanol is inferred from the section. NF-kappaB (a transcription factor) is not recorded.

records.role_detail: inhibited phospholipase D-mediated formation of phosphatidic acid (astrocytes)
records.mechanism_book_wording: inhibited phospholipase D-mediated formation of phosphatidic acid
records.quote: inhibited phospholipase D-mediated formation of phosphatidic acid, which is a mitogenic lipid messenger
records.notes: Page describes inhibition of the phospholipase D-mediated formation of phosphatidic acid; direct enzyme inhibition is not stated. Enzyme class inferred from the name.

records.role_detail: chronic ethanol feeding in mice, caspase-3 activation concomitant with inflammatory processes
records.mechanism_book_wording: the activation of a key proteolytic enzyme in this process, caspase-3
records.quote: Immunohistochemical findings in mice, fed chronically with ethanol, reveal that inflammatory processes occur concomitantly with caspase-3 activation
records.notes: The page reports caspase-3 activation concomitant with inflammation in ethanol-fed mice, an association rather than a stated direct action of ethanol. The book calls caspase-3 'a key proteolytic enzyme'.

records.role_detail: activation of TLR4 at low/moderate ethanol concentrations by interacting with membrane lipids (lipid rafts); molecular mechanism stated as unknown
records.mechanism_book_wording: ethanol can activate or inhibit TLR4 by interacting with membrane lipids
records.quote: It has been shown that ethanol can activate or inhibit TLR4 by interacting with membrane lipids.
records.numbers_detail: Low/moderate ethanol concentrations 10-50 mM, in the range found in the blood of social drinkers and alcoholics (PDF page 630)
records.notes: The page also says 'alcohol-induced toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) response triggers both, inflammatory processes and apoptosis'. The book says the molecular mechanism of ethanol interaction with TLR4 remains unknown, so agonist is the nearest role to 'activate'.

records.role_detail: high ethanol concentrations inhibit ethanol-induced activation of the TLR4 signalling pathway
records.mechanism_book_wording: high ethanol concentrations or lipid raft-disrupting agents (streptolysin-O or saponin) inhibit ethanol-induced activation of the TLR4 signalling pathway
records.quote: Conversely, high ethanol concentrations or lipid raft-disrupting agents (streptolysin-O or saponin) inhibit ethanol-induced activation of the TLR4 signalling pathway
records.notes: Statement is that high concentrations inhibit the pathway; no numeric value is given for 'high'. Streptolysin-O and saponin are named as lipid raft-disrupting agents acting on the pathway, not on TLR4 itself, so no separate records were written for them.

chapter_notes: Review-style chapter on ethanol effects in astrocytes; no Ki, IC50 or other potency values are given, only the 10-50 mM ethanol range for TLR4. About 8 statements naming ion channel, transporter, transcription factor or other non receptor/enzyme targets were skipped per the 2026-11-23 update (K+ channel, gap junction coupling, EAAT1/EAAT2 expression, glutamate transport, NF-kappaB, HSP70, cytokine and MCP-1 changes). Ethanol as a substrate of alcohol dehydrogenase, cytochrome P450 2E1, catalase and glutamine synthetase (no direction stated) was not recorded. PDF pages 631-636 are the reference list and were not mined. Many target classes and roles are inferred from enzyme or receptor names and are flagged in notes.
